facts.text: The grey shrikethrush, once commonly known as the grey thrush, is a songbird found across Australasia.
facts.quote: The grey shrikethrush or grey shrike-thrush (Colluricincla harmonica), formerly commonly known as grey thrush, is a songbird of Australasia.

facts.text: It is common across most of Australia, only absent from the driest inland deserts.
facts.quote: It is moderately common to common in most parts of Australia, but absent from the driest of the inland deserts.

facts.text: The grey shrikethrush is also found in New Guinea.
facts.quote: moderately common to common in most parts of Australia, but absent from the driest of the inland deserts. It is also found in New Guinea.

facts.text: In casual conversation, locals usually just call it the thrush.
facts.quote: The grey shrikethrush — usually just thrush in casual conversation — is of medium size (about 24 cm or 9.4 in long)

facts.text: It is a medium-sized bird of about 24 cm, without bright colours.
facts.quote: is of medium size (about 24 cm or 9.4 in long) and lacks bright colours.

facts.text: Its song is a recognizable ringing melody.
facts.quote: lacks bright colours. It has a recognizable ringing melody.

facts.text: One population of the grey shrikethrush lives in Tasmania and the islands of Bass Strait.
facts.quote: C. h. strigata – Swainson, 1838: Originally described as a separate species. Found in Tasmania and the islands in the Bass Strait (Australia)

facts.text: Another population occurs in eastern New Guinea, Torres Strait islands and north-eastern Australia.
facts.quote: Found in eastern New Guinea, islands in the Torres Strait and north-eastern Australia

facts.text: The grey shrikethrush is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.
facts.quote: The grey shrikethrush is evaluated as least concern on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.
